#!/bin/bash
# Flux batch script converted from Slurm

# NOTE: Run with: flux batch <this_script>

# Slurm resources:
#   -A yqs@v100
#   --job-name=TravailGPU
#   -C v100-32g
#   --qos=qos_gpu-t3
#   --output=TravailGPU%j.out
#   --error=TravailGPU%j.err
#   --nodes=1
#   --ntasks=1
#   --gres=gpu:1
#   --cpus-per-task=10
#   --hint=nomultithread
#   --time=20:00:00

#flux: --job-name=TravailGPU
#flux: -N 1
#flux: -n 1
#flux: -c 10
#flux: --time-limit=20h

# Omitted Slurm option: --gres=gpu:1
# Flux GPU requests are site/config dependent (often via custom resource types).
# Performance implication: job may start without a GPU, causing failure or severe slowdown.

# Omitted Slurm option: -C v100-32g (constraint)
# Flux constraints/feature selection are site-specific; no portable equivalent.
# Performance implication: job may land on non-V100 nodes or the wrong GPU memory size, reducing performance or causing failures.

# Omitted Slurm option: --qos=qos_gpu-t3
# Flux QoS/priority mappings are site-specific; no portable equivalent.
# Performance implication: job may have different priority/limits than intended, affecting wait time or eligibility.

# Omitted Slurm option: -A yqs@v100 (account)
# Flux accounting/project selection is site-specific; no portable equivalent.
# Performance implication: job may be charged to a default account or be rejected by policy.

# Omitted Slurm option: --hint=nomultithread
# Flux SMT/hyperthreading control is site/config dependent; no portable equivalent.
# Performance implication: CPU placement may include SMT threads, affecting performance/variability.

# Omitted Slurm options: --output/--error with %j token
# Slurm's %j token (job id) is not portable in Flux output/error directives.
# Performance implication: none, but logs may overwrite/collide unless you choose unique filenames.

module purge
module load pytorch-gpu/py3/1.10.1

# Slurm used srun; under Flux, use flux-run.
flux run -n 1 -c 10 python -u train_gym.py

reasons: The original Slurm job required 1 GPU (`--gres=gpu:1`) but the Flux resource section does not request any GPU resources; on GPU-managed systems this may allocate CPU-only resources and the job may fail or run much slower.

The original Slurm job specified account/QoS/constraints (`-A yqs@v100`, `--qos=qos_gpu-t3`, `-C v100-32g`) but the Flux resource section has no queue/account/constraint selection; on sites where these affect eligibility/limits or hardware selection, scheduling behavior may differ or the job may be rejected.

inputs.script:
#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH -A yqs@v100
#SBATCH --job-name=TravailGPU # nom du job
#SBATCH -C v100-32g # reserver des GPU 16 Go seulement
#SBATCH --qos=qos_gpu-t3 # QoS
#SBATCH --output=TravailGPU%j.out # fichier de sortie (%j = job ID)
#SBATCH --error=TravailGPU%j.err # fichier d’erreur (%j = job ID)
#SBATCH --nodes=1 # reserver 1 nœud
#SBATCH --ntasks=1 # reserver 4 taches (ou processus MPI)
#SBATCH --gres=gpu:1 # reserver 4 GPU
##SBATCH --partition=gpu_p4
##SBATCH --cpus-per-task=6 #server 10 CPU par tache (et memoire associee)
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=10 #server 10 CPU par tache (et memoire associee)
#SBATCH --hint=nomultithread # desactiver l’hyperthreading
#SBATCH --time=20:00:00

module purge # nettoyer les modules herites par defaut
module load pytorch-gpu/py3/1.10.1 # charger les modules
srun python -u train_gym.py #OVERRIDE IN CONFIG
#srun python -u train_dm_custom.py #upright # executer son script
